BeforeSideTurnEndVeryEarly.maps_to: on_player_turn_end_very_early (sts2_rl/relics/orichalcum.py) -- the VeryEarly phase of HookSystem's on_player_turn_end walk (sts2_rl/hooks.py:36-38, 153-180)
BeforeSideTurnEndVeryEarly.issue: Closed 2026-07-27: the phase passes are real. `HookSystem._each` walks the four phases very_early -> early -> plain -> late as COMPLETE separate listener passes whenever any current listener declares a phase variant of that hook (sts2_rl/hooks.py:36-38, 153-180), which is what Hook.cs's 24 multi-pass dispatchers do. sts2_rl/relics/orichalcum.py's `on_player_turn_end_very_early` is the snapshot's real home. WAS: the check moved into the plain slot and became order-dependent.

BeforeSideTurnEnd.maps_to: on_player_turn_end (sts2_rl/relics/orichalcum.py) -- the PLAIN BeforeSideTurnEnd pass, run after the very_early snapshot
BeforeSideTurnEnd.issue: Closed 2026-07-27: the guarantee this rollup lost is back. The grant itself was already faithful (6 unpowered Block to the owner); what was missing was the assurance that the snapshot had already happened. sts2_rl/relics/orichalcum.py now takes the snapshot in `on_player_turn_end_very_early` and grants in the plain `on_player_turn_end`, and HookSystem._each runs very_early / early / plain / late as COMPLETE separate listener passes (sts2_rl/hooks.py:36-38, 153-180) -- Hook.cs:1238-1261's three BeforeTurnEnd sub-slots. C#'s `ShouldTrigger = false` before granting (Orichalcum.cs:62) is mirrored by the port clearing `_should_trigger` in the plain slot.

BeforeSideTurnStart.rationale: Orichalcum.cs:68-76 clears ShouldTrigger at turn start, i.e. it discards a snapshot that BeforeSideTurnEnd did not consume (the case where the turn ended without the plain phase running -- a won fight). The sim holds no flag between the two halves: the snapshot and the grant are one expression, so there is nothing to go stale and nothing to reset. PROMPT.md bug class 13 asks for the first READER of the stale field; here the field does not exist. Recorded as faithful rather than deliberate-divergence because no state and no observable differ -- the missing reset is a consequence of G1's collapse, not an independent divergence, and .superpowers/sdd/content-relic-sweeps.md's Sweep A correctly does not list orichalcum as holding any state. Rule 7: the sweeps document is unhashed here. Matches audit/records/relic/fake_orichalcum.json's BeforeSideTurnStart verdict for the identical override (binding rule 3).

guards.what: G1 (LIVE): the deliberate two-phase VeryEarly-then-plain structure is collapsed into one method, so a plain-phase Block granter that runs first switches Orichalcum off
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-27: the phase passes are real. `HookSystem._each` walks the four phases very_early -> early -> plain -> late as COMPLETE separate listener passes whenever any current listener declares a phase variant of that hook (sts2_rl/hooks.py:36-38, 153-180), which is what Hook.cs's 24 multi-pass dispatchers do. sts2_rl/relics/orichalcum.py now overrides `on_player_turn_end_very_early` to snapshot `player.block > 0` into `_should_trigger` and keeps the grant in the plain `on_player_turn_end` -- Orichalcum.cs:44-56 / :58-66, whose own doc comment says the VeryEarly phase exists so the check precedes PlatingPower. The snapshot therefore precedes EVERY plain-phase listener, so relic/cloak_clasp and relic/ripple_basin can no longer switch it off by pickup order. WAS: both halves sat in one flat on_player_turn_end walk in registration order.

guards.what: N1: BlockVar(6m, ValueProp.Unpowered) (Orichalcum.cs:21) passed as the whole DynamicVar to CreatureCmd.GainBlock (:64) vs BLOCK = 6 with props=ValueProp.UNPOWERED (orichalcum.py:20, :25)
guards.rationale: Orichalcum.cs contains no AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension call, so 6 is the pinned non-ascension value. The ValueProp travels with the var in C#, which is why the port has to pass props explicitly; BlockCmd.apply skips the additive/multiplicative modifier chain unless `is_powered_attack(props)` (cmds.py:143-151), and ValueProp.UNPOWERED alone lacks MOVE so it is skipped. EXECUTED (relic_probes_b10.py orichalcum): with 5 Dexterity on the player the grant is still exactly 6. Rule 7: cmds.py is unhashed here.

Complementary tests over a quantity that is never negative -- CreatureCmd's block absorption floors at 0 and cmds.py:148 clamps a grant with `max(0, amount)` -- so `not (block > 0)` and `block == 0` agree everywhere. EXECUTED (relic_probes_b10.py orichalcum): with 1 Block already on the player the relic grants nothing, leaving 1. Rule 7: cmds.py is unhashed here.

guards.what: N3: `participants.Contains(base.Owner.Creature)` on the VeryEarly and turn-start halves (Orichalcum.cs:46, :70) but NOT on the plain BeforeSideTurnEnd half (:58-66)
guards.rationale: PROMPT.md bug class 15 says to list both guard sets side by side whenever the sim collapses two C# hooks into one method, because the collapse applies the UNION. Done: the union here is `participants.Contains(owner)` AND `Block > 0`, and the sim's on_player_turn_end is dispatched once per player turn for the player (hooks.py's player-scoped walk), so the participants clause -- a multiplayer extra-turn filter -- is structurally satisfied and adds nothing. C# can safely omit it on the plain half because ShouldTrigger is only ever set by the guarded half. So unlike relic/unsettling_lamp's G3, this collapse's union is not observable; the collapse's real cost is G1's phase ordering. Rule 7: hooks.py and relics/unsettling_lamp.py are unhashed here.
